7-1.bio:
Sts. Kosmas and Damian of Rome were brothers and physicians of the third century who healed the sick freely in the name of Christ, accepting no payment, for which they are counted among the Holy Unmercenaries. Their charity and their faith drew many to the Church, and according to tradition they ended their lives as martyrs.

They are distinguished in the calendar from the other holy Unmercenaries of the same names honored in November and October. Physicians and the sick alike seek their intercession. They are commemorated on July 1.
7-1.desc: Holy Unmercenary Physicians Cosmas and Damian of Rome.
7-1.name: Kosmas and Damian of Rome

7-1.bio:
St. Peter the Patrician was a nobleman and military officer at the court of Constantinople in the late eighth century. Tradition relates that after being taken captive in war and delivered from prison, he renounced his rank and wealth and entered the monastic life.

He lived in humility and strict asceticism at the monastery of Evandros, hiding his former dignity, and reposed in peace.
7-1.desc: Venerable Peter the Patrician, a court official of Constantinople who became a monk.
7-1.name: Peter the Patrician of Constantinople

7-1.bio:
St. Leon the Hermit is remembered in the Synaxarion as an ascetic who withdrew from the world to live in solitude, prayer and fasting. Little is recorded of his life beyond his ascetic labors.

He reposed in peace and is commemorated together with the other saints of this day.
7-1.desc: Venerable Leon the Hermit, an ascetic who reposed in peace.
7-1.name: Leon the Hermit

7-1.bio:
St. Mavrikios (Maurice) is commemorated on this day as a martyr who confessed Christ before the pagan authorities and endured torments rather than deny his faith.

The Synaxarion preserves his name and his martyric end; tradition relates that he was put to death for his confession.
7-1.desc: Holy Martyr Mavrikios, who suffered for Christ.
7-1.name: Mavrikios the Martyr

7-1.bio:
St. Konstantinos the Wonderworker is venerated in Cyprus, where tradition relates that he came with a company of ascetics and confessed Christ. He and those with him suffered martyrdom for the faith.

He is honored as a wonderworker, and his memory has long been kept in the local Church of Cyprus.
7-1.desc: Holy Martyr Konstantinos the Wonderworker of Cyprus and his companions.
7-1.name: Konstantinos the Wonderworker and those with him

7-1.bio:
The Twenty-Five Martyrs of Nicomedia were Christians who refused to sacrifice to idols during the persecutions of the early Church. Tradition relates that they were burned alive for their confession of Christ.

They are commemorated together as a company of confessors who preferred death to apostasy.
7-1.desc: The Holy Twenty-Five Martyrs who suffered by fire in Nicomedia.
7-1.name: Twenty-Five Martyrs of Nicomedia

7-10.bio:
St. Anthony of the Kiev Caves is honored as the father of monasticism in the lands of Rus. Born at Lyubech, he received the monastic tonsure on Mount Athos, and returning north he settled in a cave above the Dnieper River near Kiev, where his holiness drew disciples and the great Monastery of the Caves took root.

With his disciple St. Theodosius he set the pattern of monastic life that shaped the piety of Rus for centuries. He reposed in 1073 and is commemorated on July 10.
7-10.desc: Venerable Anthony of the Kiev Far Caves, founder of monasticism in Rus′ (†1073).
7-10.name: Anthony of the Kiev Caves

7-10.bio:
The Forty-Five Holy Martyrs of Nicopolis in Armenia confessed Christ during the persecution of the Emperor Licinius, around the year 319. Presenting themselves openly as Christians, they were imprisoned and endured harsh sufferings, encouraging one another in prayer and psalmody, and were finally put to death by fire.

Their shared confession, offered freely and together, has made them an image of the strength of the faithful united in Christ. They are commemorated on July 10.
7-10.desc: The Forty-Five Holy Martyrs of Nicopolis in Armenia, martyred under Licinius (c. 319).
7-10.name: Forty-Five Holy Martyrs of Nicopolis

7-10.bio:
In the Greek Orthodox tradition, those who bear the name Amalia keep their name day on July 10, together with the commemoration of the Forty-Five Holy Martyrs of Nicopolis. The name, of old Germanic origin, carries the sense of industriousness and care, and came into Greek usage in more recent centuries.

On this day those named Amalia and Amelie are remembered in the prayers of the Church along with the holy martyrs, whose steadfast confession of Christ sanctifies the day. The commemoration is kept on July 10.
7-10.desc: Name day for Amalia and Amelie in the Greek Orthodox tradition, commemorated with the Martyrs of Nicopolis.
7-10.name: Amalia

7-10.bio:
St. Bianor was a Christian of Pisidia who was tortured for refusing to sacrifice to idols. Tradition relates that Silouanos, seeing his courage, confessed Christ as well.

Both were beheaded and received the crown of martyrdom together.
7-10.desc: Holy Martyrs Bianor and Silouanos of Pisidia.
7-10.name: Bianor and Silouanos

7-10.bio:
St. Apollonios was a Christian of Sardis in Lydia who refused to swear by the fortune of the emperor. Brought before the governor at Iconium, he confessed Christ openly.

Tradition relates that he was crucified for his faith.
7-10.desc: Holy Martyr Apollonios of Sardis, crucified for Christ.
7-10.name: Apollonios of Sardis

7-10.bio:
The Ten Thousand Fathers were monks of the Egyptian desert who were slain in the time of Patriarch Theophilos of Alexandria, who had them accused of Origenism. Tradition relates that they were killed by fire and sword in their monasteries.

They are commemorated as a company of holy ascetics who suffered unjustly.
7-10.desc: The Holy Ten Thousand Fathers martyred in the desert of Nitria.
7-10.name: Ten Thousand Fathers of Nitria

7-10.bio:
Sts. Parthenios and Eumenios were brothers from Pigaidakia in Crete who lived as ascetics and refounded the Monastery of Koudoumas on the southern coast of the island. They lived in the nineteenth and early twentieth centuries.

Both reposed in peace and were glorified by the Church; their relics are honored at Koudoumas.
7-10.desc: Venerable Parthenios and Eumenios, founders of the Koudoumas Monastery in Crete.
7-10.name: Parthenios and Eumenios of Koudoumas

7-10.bio:
On this day the Monastery of Vatopedi on Mount Athos commemorates together all the saints who lived and labored within its walls: founders, ascetics, hierarchs and martyrs.

The synaxis gathers the many holy fathers of Vatopedi into one celebration.
7-10.desc: Synaxis of all the Saints of the Holy Monastery of Vatopedi on Mount Athos.
7-10.name: Synaxis of the Saints of Vatopedi

7-11.bio:
St. Euphemia the All-Praised was a virgin martyr of Chalcedon who suffered for Christ during the persecutions at the turn of the fourth century, enduring torture and death rather than sacrifice to idols. Her principal feast is kept on September 16.

On July 11 the Church commemorates the miracle wrought through her relics at the Fourth Ecumenical Council at Chalcedon in 451, when, according to tradition, the definition of the Orthodox faith placed in her tomb was received and confirmed, sealing the true confession of Christ. For this she is called the confirmer of Orthodoxy, and is honored on July 11.
7-11.name: Euphemia the All-Praised

7-11.bio:
St. Olga was the wife of Prince Igor of Kiev and ruled Rus' after his death in the tenth century. She traveled to Constantinople, where she was baptized with the name Helen, and returned to Kiev as the first Christian ruler of her people.

Though her son remained a pagan, her grandson Vladimir would later baptize all of Rus'. She reposed in peace and is honored as Equal-to-the-Apostles.
7-11.desc: Holy Equal-to-the-Apostles Olga, Princess of Kiev, grandmother of St. Vladimir.
7-11.name: Olga of Kiev

7-11.bio:
St. Sophrony (Sakharov) was born in Moscow in 1896 and became a monk on Mount Athos, where he was the disciple of St. Silouan the Athonite. He later founded the Monastery of St. John the Baptist in Essex, England.

He reposed in 1993 and was glorified by the Ecumenical Patriarchate in 2019. His writings on prayer and the person of Christ are read throughout the Orthodox world.
7-11.desc: Venerable Sophrony (Sakharov) of Essex, disciple of St. Silouan the Athonite.
7-11.name: Sophrony of Essex

7-11.bio:
St. Nektarios was born in Vryoulla in Asia Minor and, having been drawn into apostasy in his youth, repented and became a monk in the Skete of St. Anne on Mount Athos. Tradition relates that he returned to his homeland to confess Christ openly.

He was beheaded in 1820 and is honored among the New Martyrs of the Holy Mountain.
7-11.desc: New Monastic Martyr Nektarios of Vryoulla, who suffered in Asia Minor.
7-11.name: Nektarios of Vryoulla

7-11.bio:
St. Nikodemos was from Elbasan in Albania and had fallen into apostasy. Tradition relates that he repented on Mount Athos, became a monk, and returned to confess Christ before those who had known him.

He was beheaded in 1722 and is honored among the New Martyrs.
7-11.desc: New Monastic Martyr Nikodemos of Elbasan in Albania.
7-11.name: Nikodemos of Elbasan

7-11.bio:
St. Kindeos was a priest in Pamphylia during the persecution of Diocletian. Denounced as a Christian, he was condemned to be burned.

Tradition relates that he walked calmly to the fire and gave up his soul in prayer.
7-11.name: Kindeos the Presbyter

7-11.bio:
St. Nikodemos was an ascetic of Vatopedi Monastery on Mount Athos in the fourteenth century. He is remembered as the elder who received the young Gregory Palamas and guided him in the life of prayer.

He reposed in peace and is honored among the saints of the Holy Mountain.
7-11.desc: Venerable Nikodemos of Vatopedi, spiritual father of St. Gregory Palamas.
7-11.name: Nikodemos of Vatopedi

7-12.bio:
St. Paisios was born in Farasa of Cappadocia in 1924 and grew up in Konitsa in Epirus. After military service he became a monk, living on Mount Athos, at Sinai and finally in the cell of Panagouda near Koutloumousiou, where he received countless pilgrims with discernment and love.

He reposed in 1994 at the convent of St. John the Theologian at Souroti near Thessaloniki, where his grave is a place of pilgrimage. He was glorified by the Ecumenical Patriarchate in 2015.
7-12.desc: Venerable Paisios the Athonite, elder of Mount Athos and beloved spiritual father of modern Greece.
7-12.name: Paisios the Athonite

7-12.bio:
St. Veronica is identified by tradition with the woman of the Gospel who had suffered from an issue of blood for twelve years and was healed when she touched the hem of the Lord's garment in faith. Tradition relates that she came from Caesarea Philippi.

She lived the rest of her life in piety and thanksgiving, and is honored as a holy woman of the apostolic age.
7-12.desc: St. Veronica, the woman healed of the issue of blood by touching the hem of Christ's garment.
7-12.name: Veronica the Woman with the Issue of Blood

7-12.bio:
St. Michael Maleinos was born to a noble family of Cappadocia in the tenth century and became a monk on Mount Kyminas in Bithynia. He was renowned for asceticism and was the spiritual father of St. Athanasios, founder of the Great Lavra on Mount Athos.

He reposed in peace, having guided many in the monastic life.
7-12.desc: Venerable Michael Maleinos, spiritual father of St. Athanasios of Athos.
7-12.name: Michael Maleinos

7-12.bio:
St. Serapion the New was a Christian who confessed Christ during the persecutions of the third century. Tradition relates that he was tortured and finally burned for his faith.

He is called 'the New' to distinguish him from earlier martyrs of the same name.
7-12.desc: Holy Martyr Serapion the New, burned for Christ.
7-12.name: Serapion the New

7-12.bio:
St. Andrew the Stratelates was a Roman military commander who confessed Christ together with his soldiers, among them Herakleios, Faustus and Menas. Tradition relates that they were slain by the sword in a mountain pass.

They are commemorated together as a company of soldier martyrs.
7-12.desc: Holy Martyrs Andrew the Stratelates, Herakleios, Faustus, Menas and their company.
7-12.name: Andrew the Stratelates and those with him

7-12.bio:
Saints Proclus and Hilary were natives of the village of Kallipi near Ancyra in Galatia who suffered during the persecution of the Emperor Trajan. Proclus, the elder, was arrested first and endured torture with such steadfastness that his nephew Hilary, moved by his example, openly confessed Christ as well.

Both were put to death for the faith, Proclus by arrows and Hilary by the sword, according to the synaxaria. They are commemorated together on July 12.
7-12.desc: Holy Martyrs Proclus and Hilary of Kallipi near Ancyra.
7-12.name: Proclus and Hilary of Ancyra

7-13.bio:
St. Stephen the Sabbaite was a monk of the renowned Lavra of St. Savas in the Judean desert, living in the eighth century. Given to the monastery from childhood, he grew up in its life of prayer, was formed in its discipline, and spent his years in ascetic struggle, stillness, and love for the brethren, becoming a spiritual guide to many.

He is remembered also as a hymnographer of the Church, in the great tradition of the Lavra that nurtured him. He reposed in peace and is commemorated on July 13.
7-13.name: Stephen the Sabbaite

7-13.bio:
On July 13 the Church keeps a second synaxis in honor of the Archangel Gabriel, gathering the faithful once more to celebrate the great messenger of God. Tradition connects the feast with the dedication of a church in his name and with thanksgiving for his wonders through the centuries.

Gabriel is honored as the herald of the Incarnation, who brought the good tidings to the Theotokos, and as one of the chief commanders of the bodiless powers who stand before the throne of God. He is honored also on March 26 and, with the Archangel Michael, on November 8.
7-13.desc: Second Synaxis of the Holy Archangel Gabriel, chief of the Bodiless Powers.
7-13.name: Synaxis of the Archangel Gabriel

7-13.bio:
St. Sarah was an ascetic of the Egyptian desert who lived for many years beside a river near Sketis. Her sayings are recorded among the Sayings of the Desert Fathers, where she is remembered for her fierce struggle against temptation and her spiritual wisdom.

She reposed in peace after a long life of asceticism.
7-13.desc: Venerable Sarah, desert mother of Sketis, whose sayings are preserved among the Desert Fathers.
7-13.name: Sarah of Sketis

7-13.bio:
St. Golinduch was the wife of a Persian magus who came to believe in Christ and was baptized with the name Maria. For her faith she endured years of imprisonment and torments under the Persian king.

Tradition relates that she was miraculously delivered and ended her life in peace in the Byzantine lands.
7-13.desc: St. Golinduch of Persia, named Maria in baptism, confessor.
7-13.name: Golinduch of Persia

7-13.bio:
The Heliophotoi are a company of martyrs venerated in Cyprus, whose names are preserved in local tradition. They are said to have suffered for Christ in the early Christian centuries.

Their memory is kept in the villages of Cyprus where their relics were honored.
7-13.desc: The Holy Heliophotoi Martyrs of Cyprus.
7-13.name: Heliophotoi Martyrs of Cyprus

7-13.bio:
St. Onesiphoros is commemorated on this day as a martyr who confessed Christ during the persecutions of the early Church. Tradition relates that he was put to death for his faith.

His name is kept in the Synaxarion among the martyrs of this day.
7-13.name: Onesiphoros the Martyr

7-13.bio:
St. Nikodemos was a monk of Serbian and Greek descent who lived on Mount Athos and then founded the monasteries of Vodita and Tismana in Wallachia in the fourteenth century. He organized monastic life in the Romanian lands on the Athonite pattern.

He reposed in 1406 and is honored as a father of Romanian monasticism.
7-13.desc: Venerable Nikodemos of Tismana, founder of monasteries in Romania.
7-13.name: Nikodemos of Tismana

7-14.bio:
St. Aquila, numbered among the Seventy Apostles, was a Jewish tentmaker who with his wife Priscilla received St. Paul into their home at Corinth and shared both his trade and his labors for the Gospel. The couple are mentioned with affection in the Scriptures, and their house served as a gathering place for the Church.

According to tradition Aquila preached the Gospel and was made a bishop, ending his life in martyrdom. He is commemorated on July 14.
7-14.name: Aquila the Apostle

7-14.bio:
St. Nikodemos was born on the island of Naxos in 1749 and became a monk on Mount Athos. A man of vast learning and deep prayer, he edited the Philokalia together with St. Makarios of Corinth and wrote many works of spiritual guidance, including the Synaxarion of the saints.

He reposed in 1809 and was glorified in 1955. He is honored as a teacher of the whole Orthodox Church.
7-14.desc: Venerable Nikodemos the Hagiorite, teacher of the Church and compiler of the Philokalia.
7-14.name: Nikodemos the Hagiorite

7-14.bio:
St. Joseph was the brother of St. Theodore the Studite and became Archbishop of Thessaloniki in the early ninth century. He suffered exile and imprisonment for his defense of the holy icons and for opposing the unlawful marriage of the emperor.

He is also remembered as a hymnographer and reposed as a confessor.
7-14.desc: St. Joseph the Confessor, Archbishop of Thessaloniki, brother of St. Theodore the Studite.
7-14.name: Joseph of Thessaloniki

7-14.bio:
St. Justus was a soldier at Rome who, according to tradition, saw a vision of the Cross and came to believe in Christ. He gave his possessions to the poor and openly confessed his faith.

He was tortured and burned, and received the crown of martyrdom.
7-14.desc: Holy Martyr Justus, a Roman soldier who confessed Christ.
7-14.name: Justus the Martyr

7-14.bio:
St. Onesimos was born in Caesarea of Palestine and embraced the monastic life in his youth. Tradition relates that he lived as an ascetic near Ephesus and later founded a monastery at Magnesia, where he was known for his gifts of healing.

He reposed in peace in the fourth century.
7-14.desc: Venerable Onesimos the Wonderworker of Magnesia.
7-14.name: Onesimos the Wonderworker

7-14.bio:
St. Stephen was a monk of the Kiev Caves who moved north and founded a monastery at Makhrishche in the fourteenth century. He was a friend of St. Sergius of Radonezh and shared his labors in reviving monastic life.

He reposed in peace in 1406.
7-14.desc: Venerable Stephen, abbot of Makhrishche, friend of St. Sergius of Radonezh.
7-14.name: Stephen of Makhrishche

7-15.bio:
St. Vladimir, Equal-to-the-Apostles, was Great Prince of Kiev in the tenth century. Raised in paganism, he sought out the true faith, and after his envoys beheld the divine services in Constantinople he received holy baptism and in 988 led his people to the waters of the Dnieper, the baptism of Rus.

From a harsh ruler he became a father to his people, building churches, feeding the poor, and softening the laws. Through him the Orthodox faith took root in the lands of Rus. He reposed in 1015 and is commemorated on July 15.
7-15.desc: Equal-to-the-Apostles Vladimir, Great Prince of Kiev.
7-15.name: Vladimir of Kiev

7-15.bio:
St. Julitta was a noblewoman of Iconium who fled the persecution of Diocletian with her three-year-old son Kerykos. Arrested in Tarsus, she confessed Christ before the governor; the child, held on the governor's knee, cried out that he too was a Christian and was thrown down the steps to his death.

Julitta rejoiced that her son had gone before her and was herself beheaded. Mother and child are honored together, and many churches in Greece bear their names.
7-15.desc: Holy Martyrs Kerykos, a child of three years, and his mother Julitta of Iconium.
7-15.name: Kerykos and Julitta

7-15.bio:
St. Lollianos is commemorated as a martyr who confessed Christ during the persecutions of the early Church. Tradition relates that he died by the sword.

His name is preserved in the Synaxarion among the martyrs of this day.
7-15.name: Lollianos the Martyr

7-15.bio:
St. Aboudimos was a Christian of the island of Tenedos who refused to sacrifice to idols during the persecution of Diocletian. Brought before the governor, he confessed Christ boldly.

He was tortured and beheaded for his faith.
7-15.desc: Holy Martyr Aboudimos of the island of Tenedos.
7-15.name: Aboudimos of Tenedos

7-15.bio:
This day commemorates the finding of the head of St. Matrona of Chios, the fifteenth-century ascetic who founded a convent on the island and is honored as one of its patrons.

Her main feast is kept on October 20; the relic is venerated in Chios.
7-15.desc: Finding of the precious head of Venerable Matrona of Chios.
7-15.name: Finding of the Head of Matrona of Chios

7-16.bio:
St. Athenogenes was a bishop in the region of Sebaste who suffered martyrdom with a company of his disciples during the persecutions at the turn of the fourth century. Refusing to deny Christ, he strengthened his spiritual children as they went before him to death, and then received the crown of martyrdom himself.

An ancient tradition tells that as he went to his death he sang with joy, and his name is linked in the memory of the Church with the beloved evening hymn of thanksgiving at the lighting of the lamps. He is commemorated on July 16.
7-16.name: Athenogenes

7-16.bio:
St. Faustus was a Christian who confessed Christ during the persecution of Decius. Tradition relates that he was crucified and remained alive on the cross for five days before giving up his soul.

He is honored as a martyr who endured to the end.
7-16.desc: Holy Martyr Faustus, crucified for Christ.
7-16.name: Faustus the Martyr

7-16.bio:
St. Antiochos was a physician of Sebaste in Cappadocia, brother of the Martyr Platon, who traveled healing the sick and preaching Christ. Arrested, he endured tortures unharmed, and when he was beheaded, tradition relates that milk flowed instead of blood.

Seeing this, the executioner Kyriakos confessed Christ and was himself beheaded.
7-16.desc: Holy Martyrs Antiochos the Physician of Sebaste and Kyriakos, the executioner who believed.
7-16.name: Antiochos and Kyriakos the Executioner

7-16.bio:
The Fifteen Thousand Martyrs of Pisidia are commemorated as a great company of Christians who suffered for Christ in that region of Asia Minor. Tradition relates that they were put to the sword.

The Church keeps their common memory as a witness to the faith of the early Christians of Pisidia.
7-16.desc: The Holy Fifteen Thousand Martyrs who suffered in Pisidia.
7-16.name: Fifteen Thousand Martyrs of Pisidia

7-16.bio:
Sts. Anastasios and Euxitheos are commemorated together as early hierarchs of the Church of Thessaloniki. Little is recorded of their lives beyond their episcopal service.

They reposed in peace and are honored among the saints of Thessaloniki.
7-16.desc: Sts. Anastasios and Euxitheos, Bishops of Thessaloniki.
7-16.name: Anastasios and Euxitheos of Thessaloniki

7-17.bio:
St. Marina the Great Martyr was born in Antioch of Pisidia in the third century. Losing her mother as a child and raised in the countryside, she embraced Christ in her youth; when her faith became known she was seized during the persecutions, and though only about fifteen years of age she withstood interrogation, torture, and, according to tradition, the assaults of the evil one, whom she overcame by prayer, before being beheaded.

She is greatly beloved in Greece, where many churches and villages bear her name, and she is invoked as a protector of children and a help against the powers of darkness. Her feast is July 17.
7-17.name: Marina the Great Martyr

7-17.bio:
Sts. Speratos and Veronica are numbered among the Scillitan Martyrs, Christians of North Africa who were tried at Carthage in the second century and refused to swear by the emperor. Their trial is one of the earliest recorded acts of the martyrs.

They were beheaded for their confession of Christ.
7-17.desc: Holy Martyrs Speratos and Veronica, of the Scillitan martyrs of North Africa.
7-17.name: Speratos and Veronica

7-17.bio:
St. Euphrasios served as Bishop of Ionopolis on the Black Sea coast of Asia Minor. Little is recorded of his life beyond his episcopal service.

He reposed in peace and is honored among the hierarchs of the Church.
7-17.name: Euphrasios of Ionopolis

7-17.bio:
This day commemorates the translation of the relics of St. Lazarus of Mount Galesion, the eleventh-century stylite who lived near Ephesus and founded monasteries on the mountain. Educated at the Lavra of St. Savva in Palestine, he was known for asceticism and wonderworking.

His main feast is kept on November 7.
7-17.desc: Translation of the relics of Venerable Lazarus the Stylite of Mount Galesion.
7-17.name: Translation of the Relics of Lazarus of Galesion

7-18.bio:
St. Emilian was a Christian of Dorostolon on the Danube who suffered martyrdom in the fourth century, in the reign of Julian the Apostate. Moved by zeal for the true God, he entered a pagan temple and overturned the idols; when another man was blamed for the deed, he came forward and confessed it freely rather than let the innocent suffer.

For his confession of Christ he was put to death by fire, and the Church honors his honesty and courage together. He is commemorated on July 18.
7-18.name: Emilian of Dorostolum

7-18.bio:
St. Paul and the sisters Valentina and Thea were Egyptian Christians brought to Caesarea in Palestine during the persecution of Maximian in the early fourth century. When Thea was tortured, her sister Valentina overturned the pagan altar and was condemned with her.

The two sisters were burned, and Paul was beheaded after praying for the whole world; their martyrdom is described by Eusebius.
7-18.desc: Holy Martyrs Paul and the sisters Valentina and Thea of Caesarea in Palestine.
7-18.name: Paul, Valentina and Thea

7-18.bio:
St. Pambo was one of the great desert fathers of Nitria in Egypt in the fourth century, a disciple of St. Anthony the Great. Unlettered at first, he learned the Psalms and was known for his silence, his humility and his labor with his hands.

He reposed in peace, and his sayings are preserved among the Desert Fathers.
7-18.desc: Venerable Pambo the Hermit, desert father of Nitria.
7-18.name: Pambo of Egypt

7-18.bio:
St. Hyakinthos was a Christian of Amastris on the Black Sea who cut down a tree venerated by the pagans. For this he was tortured and put to death.

He is commemorated as a martyr of the early Church.
7-18.name: Hyakinthos of Amastris

7-18.bio:
St. Markellos is commemorated as a martyr who confessed Christ during the persecutions. Tradition relates that he died by fire.

His name is kept in the Synaxarion among the martyrs of this day.
7-18.name: Markellos the Martyr

7-18.bio:
Sts. Dasios and Maron are commemorated together as martyrs who confessed Christ during the persecutions of the early Church. Tradition relates that they died by the sword.

Their names are preserved in the Synaxarion.
7-18.name: Dasios and Maron

7-18.bio:
St. John the Long-Suffering was a monk of the Kiev Caves in the twelfth century who struggled for thirty years against the passions. Tradition relates that he buried himself up to the chest in the earth of his cave and remained there in prayer.

He reposed in peace, and his relics rest in the Near Caves.
7-18.desc: Venerable John the Long-Suffering, recluse of the Kiev Caves.
7-18.name: John the Long-Suffering of Kiev

7-19.bio:
St. Makrina belonged to the extraordinary Cappadocian family of saints that gave the Church St. Basil the Great and St. Gregory of Nyssa. A woman of deep piety and steadfast faith, she devoted herself to prayer and the ascetic life, and through her teaching and example the Orthodox faith was handed down within a household that produced some of the greatest fathers of the Church.

She is honored as a model of holiness lived out in family life, showing how the faith is passed from generation to generation. She is commemorated on July 19.
7-19.desc: Venerable Macrina, grandmother of Basil the Great.
7-19.name: Makrina the Elder

7-19.bio:
St. Dios was born in Antioch and lived as an ascetic before coming to Constantinople in the reign of Theodosios the Great, where he founded a monastery. Tradition relates that he was granted the gift of working miracles.

He reposed in peace in the fifth century.
7-19.desc: Venerable Dios the Wonderworker, abbot in Constantinople.
7-19.name: Dios of Antioch

7-19.bio:
St. Theodore was born in Edessa and became a monk at the Lavra of St. Savva in Palestine, where he was known for asceticism and learning. He was later consecrated Bishop of Edessa and labored to strengthen the Orthodox there.

He reposed in peace in the ninth century.
7-19.desc: St. Theodore the Sabbaite, Bishop of Edessa.
7-19.name: Theodore of Edessa

7-19.bio:
This day commemorates the uncovering of the relics of St. Seraphim of Sarov in 1903, at his glorification by the Russian Church. St. Seraphim, who reposed in 1833, is one of the most beloved of Russian saints, known for his teaching on the acquisition of the Holy Spirit.

His main feast is kept on January 2.
7-19.desc: Uncovering of the relics of Venerable Seraphim of Sarov, wonderworker.
7-19.name: Finding of the Relics of Seraphim of Sarov

7-19.bio:
The Fourth Ecumenical Council met at Chalcedon in 451 and confirmed the Orthodox faith that Christ is one Person in two natures, divine and human. Its Fathers are commemorated on the Sunday between July 13 and 19 together with the Fathers of the first six Councils.

The Church honors them as defenders of the true faith against heresy.
7-19.desc: Commemoration of the Holy Fathers of the Fourth Ecumenical Council at Chalcedon.
7-19.name: Fathers of the Fourth Ecumenical Council

7-19.bio:
St. Diokles is commemorated as an ascetic who left the world to live in prayer and fasting. Little is recorded of his life beyond his ascetic labors.

He reposed in peace.
7-19.desc: Venerable Diokles, an ascetic who reposed in peace.
7-19.name: Diokles the Venerable

7-2.bio:
St. Juvenaly was Patriarch of Jerusalem in the fifth century, shepherding the Holy City for several decades during the great christological controversies. He took part in the Third Ecumenical Council at Ephesus and the Fourth at Chalcedon, standing with the Orthodox faith in Christ, and during his episcopate the see of Jerusalem was honored as a patriarchate.

Tradition also associates him with the events surrounding the veneration of the Dormition of the Theotokos. He reposed in peace after a long ministry, and is commemorated on July 2.
7-2.name: Juvenaly of Jerusalem

7-2.bio:
This feast commemorates the placing of the precious Robe of the Most Holy Theotokos in the church of Blachernae in Constantinople during the fifth century, in the reign of Emperor Leo the Great. Tradition relates that the Robe had been kept by pious Christians in the Holy Land before being brought to the imperial city.

The Robe was regarded as a protection of the city, and its deposition has been celebrated ever since as a feast of the Mother of God.
7-2.desc: Deposition of the precious Robe of the Most Holy Theotokos in the church of Blachernae, Constantinople.
7-2.name: Deposition of the Robe of the Theotokos

7-2.bio:
St. John (Maximovitch) was born in Russia in 1896 and served as a bishop of the Russian Church abroad in Shanghai, Western Europe and finally San Francisco, where he reposed in 1966. He was renowned for his severe asceticism, ceaseless prayer and care for orphans and the poor.

He was glorified as a saint in 1994, and his incorrupt relics rest in the cathedral in San Francisco. He is honored throughout the Orthodox world as a wonderworker of our own time.
7-2.desc: St. John Maximovitch, Archbishop of Shanghai and San Francisco, wonderworker of the twentieth century.
7-2.name: John Maximovitch of San Francisco

7-2.bio:
St. Lambros was one of the New Martyrs of Samothrace who confessed Christ before the Ottoman authorities in the nineteenth century. Tradition relates that he was put to death for refusing to deny his faith.

He is honored on the island of Samothrace together with the other New Martyrs who shared his confession.
7-2.desc: New Martyr Lambros of Samothrace, who suffered under the Ottomans.
7-2.name: Lambros the New Martyr of Samothrace

7-2.bio:
St. Kointos (Quintus) was a Christian of Phrygia in the third century who gave alms generously and was known for healing the sick. Brought before the pagan authorities, he confessed Christ and was tortured, but survived his sufferings.

Tradition relates that he continued to work healings after his confession and reposed in peace, honored as a confessor and wonderworker.
7-2.desc: Holy Confessor and Wonderworker Kointos of Phrygia.
7-2.name: Kointos the Confessor

7-2.bio:
St. Photios was a monk from Monemvasia in the Peloponnese who was appointed Metropolitan of Kiev and All Russia in the early fifteenth century. He labored to restore church order and defended the Church against heresies and disorder.

He reposed in 1431 and is honored as a shepherd who united the Greek and Russian Churches in his person.
7-2.desc: St. Photios, Metropolitan of Kiev and Moscow, a Greek from Monemvasia.
7-2.name: Photios of Moscow

7-2.bio:
St. Stephen the Great ruled Moldavia from 1457 and defended his Orthodox land for decades against invading armies. He built and endowed many churches and monasteries, including on Mount Athos, in thanksgiving for his victories.

He reposed in 1504 and was glorified by the Romanian Church, which honors him as a defender of Orthodoxy.
7-2.desc: Right-believing Stephen the Great, Prince of Moldavia, defender of the faith and builder of monasteries.
7-2.name: Stephen the Great of Moldavia

7-20.bio:
The Holy Prophet Elijah the Tishbite lived in the ninth century before Christ, in the days of King Ahab of Israel. Zealous for the Lord against the worship of Baal, he shut the heavens by his prayer, was fed by ravens at the brook Cherith, raised the son of the widow of Zarephath, and called down fire from heaven on Mount Carmel. He was taken up alive toward heaven in a chariot of fire, leaving his mantle to his disciple Elisha.

Elijah appeared with Moses beside Christ at the Transfiguration. In Greece his chapels crown countless mountaintops, and his feast on July 20 is kept with great devotion.
7-20.desc: Holy Prophet Elijah the Tishbite, taken up to heaven in a fiery chariot.
7-20.name: Elijah the Prophet

7-20.bio:
St. Abramios was a disciple of St. Sergius of Radonezh who withdrew to the wilderness near Galich in northern Russia, where he founded several monasteries. He labored in preaching to the local people.

He reposed in peace in the fourteenth century.
7-20.desc: Venerable Abramios of Galich and Chukhloma, disciple of St. Sergius of Radonezh.
7-20.name: Abramios of Galich

7-20.bio:
St. Maria (Skobtsova) was a Russian nun in Paris who devoted herself to the poor, refugees and, during the war, the persecuted Jews. She was arrested with her son Yuri, the priest Dimitri Klepinin and Ilya Fondaminsky, and died in the Ravensbruck camp in 1945.

They were glorified by the Ecumenical Patriarchate in 2004 and are commemorated together.
7-20.desc: Synaxis of the Russian saints who died in France: Mother Maria of Paris and her companions.
7-20.name: Maria Skobtsova and those with her

7-20.bio:
St. Athanasios was abbot of the monastery of Brest-Litovsk in the seventeenth century and a fearless defender of Orthodoxy against the Unia. Arrested on false charges, he was shot in 1648.

This day commemorates the uncovering of his relics; his main feast is September 5.
7-20.desc: Hieromartyr Athanasios, abbot of Brest, who suffered for Orthodoxy.
7-20.name: Athanasios of Brest

7-21.bio:
St. Symeon the Fool for Christ was a sixth-century ascetic of Syria. After long years of prayer and struggle in the desert by the Dead Sea with his companion St. John, he was called to a stranger path: entering the city of Emesa, he feigned madness, enduring mockery and blows while secretly feeding the poor, converting sinners, and working hidden wonders.

His folly concealed great holiness, revealed only after his repose. He is honored as one of the first and greatest of the fools for Christ, and is commemorated on July 21.
7-21.desc: Venerable Symeon the Holy Fool for Christ.
7-21.name: Symeon the Fool for Christ

7-21.bio:
St. Parthenios was Bishop of Radovisdion in the region of Arta in Epirus in the seventeenth century. He was known for his holiness and care for his flock during the Ottoman period.

He reposed in peace, and his relics are honored in Epirus.
7-21.desc: St. Parthenios, Bishop of Radovisdion in Epirus.
7-21.name: Parthenios of Radovisdion

7-21.bio:
Sts. Theophilos, Trophimos and thirteen companions were Christians of Lycia who refused to sacrifice to idols during the persecution of Diocletian. Tradition relates that they were tortured and beheaded together.

They are commemorated as one company of martyrs.
7-21.desc: Holy Martyrs Theophilos, Trophimos and thirteen others who suffered in Lycia.
7-21.name: Theophilos, Trophimos and Thirteen Martyrs

7-21.bio:
Sts. Justus and Matthew are commemorated together as martyrs who confessed Christ during the persecutions of the early Church. Tradition relates that they died by the sword.

Their names are preserved in the Synaxarion.
7-21.name: Justus and Matthew

7-21.bio:
St. Eugenios is commemorated as a martyr who confessed Christ during the persecutions. Tradition relates that he died by the sword.

His name is kept in the Synaxarion among the martyrs of this day.
7-21.name: Eugenios the Martyr

7-21.bio:
St. Onouphrios the Silent was a monk of the Kiev Caves who took upon himself the ascetic labor of silence, speaking with no one and giving himself wholly to prayer.

He reposed in peace, and his relics rest in the Near Caves.
7-21.desc: Venerable Onouphrios the Silent of the Kiev Caves.
7-21.name: Onouphrios the Silent

7-22.bio:
St. Mary Magdalene, the Myrrh-Bearer and Equal-to-the-Apostles, was healed by the Lord of seven demons and thereafter followed Him from Galilee, ministering to Him from her own means. She stood by the Cross when most had fled, and coming early to the tomb she was among the first to behold the risen Christ, who sent her to announce the Resurrection to the Apostles.

For this she is honored as an apostle to the apostles. According to tradition she later preached the Gospel and reposed in Ephesus, and her relics were brought in time to Constantinople. The Church commemorates her on July 22 and with the Myrrh-Bearers after Pascha.
7-22.name: Mary Magdalene

7-22.bio:
St. Phokas was bishop of Sinope on the Black Sea, a shepherd of the early Church renowned for his holiness, who completed his ministry as a hieromartyr, suffering death for his confession of Christ during the Roman persecutions.

He has long been honored as a protector of seafarers, and sailors of the Black Sea and beyond kept his memory with special devotion. Alongside his principal feast in September, the Church also commemorates him on July 22, the day associated with the translation of his holy relics.
7-22.name: Phokas of Sinope

7-22.bio:
St. Markella was a young virgin of the island of Chios, honored by tradition as a martyr of purity. Raised in the faith by a devout mother whom she lost early, she lived in prayer and modesty. When her own father, given over to sinful passion, pursued her, she fled; refusing to yield, she was put to death by his hand and received the crown of martyrdom.

At the place of her martyrdom on Chios a shrine and holy spring bear her memory, and many pilgrims seek her intercession there. She is the patroness of Chios, and her feast is kept on July 22.
7-22.name: Markella of Chios

7-22.bio:
St. Menelaos is commemorated as an ascetic and abbot who lived in Gaul in the eighth century. Tradition relates that he founded a monastery in the Auvergne and guided many in the monastic life.

He reposed in peace. His day is kept by those who bear this ancient Greek name.
7-22.name: Menelaos the Venerable

7-23.bio:
The Holy Prophet Ezekiel was a priest of Israel carried into the Babylonian captivity in the sixth century before Christ. By the river Chebar he beheld the awesome vision of the glory of the Lord upon the chariot of the cherubim, and he prophesied to the exiles both judgment and consolation, including the vision of the dry bones brought to life, a foreshadowing of the resurrection.

The Church reads his prophecy of the shut gate as a figure of the Ever-Virgin Theotokos. He is commemorated on July 23.
7-23.name: Ezekiel the Prophet

7-23.bio:
St. Pelagia was a nun of the Kechrovouni convent on the island of Tinos. In 1822 the Theotokos appeared to her in a vision and directed her to the place where the icon of the Annunciation lay buried; the icon was found in 1823 and the great church of the Evangelistria was built there.

She reposed in 1834 and was glorified in 1970. Her cell is venerated at Kechrovouni.
7-23.desc: Venerable Pelagia of Tinos, to whom the Theotokos revealed the icon of the Evangelistria.
7-23.name: Pelagia of Tinos

7-23.bio:
St. Apollinarios was, according to tradition, a disciple of the Apostle Peter who was sent to Ravenna in Italy as its first bishop. He preached Christ there for many years, enduring repeated persecution and exile.

He died from the beatings of the pagans and is honored as a hieromartyr and patron of Ravenna.
7-23.desc: Hieromartyr Apollinarios, Bishop of Ravenna, disciple of the Apostle Peter.
7-23.name: Apollinarios of Ravenna

7-23.bio:
St. Anna of Leukadion was a pious woman of Constantinople who, according to tradition, left the world after being widowed and lived in asceticism in the district of Leukadion.

She reposed in peace and is honored among the holy women of the imperial city.
7-23.desc: Venerable Anna of Leukadion, ascetic of Constantinople.
7-23.name: Anna of Leukadion

7-23.bio:
St. Vitalis was a Christian of Milan who, according to tradition, encouraged a martyr at Ravenna and was himself arrested. He was tortured and buried alive for his confession of Christ.

He is honored as a martyr of Ravenna, where a great church bears his name.
7-23.name: Vitalis of Ravenna

7-23.bio:
These martyrs were Christian soldiers and captives of the Byzantine army who fell into the hands of the pagan Bulgarians in the early ninth century, in the time of Emperor Nikephoros. Refusing to renounce Christ, they were put to death.

The Church keeps their common memory as confessors of the faith.
7-23.desc: The Holy Martyrs put to death by the Bulgarians in the ninth century.
7-23.name: Martyrs Slain by the Bulgarians

7-24.bio:
St. Christina the Great Martyr suffered for Christ at Tyre in the third century. Born to a prominent pagan family and kept apart by her father, she came to knowledge of the one true God, and destroyed the idols of gold and silver set before her, giving the fragments to the poor. For this she endured imprisonment and cruel tortures at the hands of successive judges, remaining unshaken until she received the crown of martyrdom.

Her name proclaims her belonging to Christ, and her courage in her youth has been honored throughout the centuries. Her feast is July 24.
7-24.name: Christina the Great Martyr

7-24.bio:
St. Athenagoras was an Athenian philosopher of the second century who, tradition relates, came to faith in Christ while studying the Scriptures in order to refute them. He wrote a Plea for the Christians addressed to the emperor, defending the faith against slander, and a treatise on the resurrection.

He is honored as one of the early apologists of the Church.
7-24.desc: St. Athenagoras the Athenian, philosopher and apologist of the faith.
7-24.name: Athenagoras the Apologist

7-24.bio:
Sts. Boris and Gleb were sons of St. Vladimir of Kiev who, after their father's death in 1015, refused to raise arms against their elder brother Svyatopolk, though he sought their lives. They accepted death in the spirit of Christ rather than shed the blood of their kin.

They were the first saints glorified in Rus' and are honored as passion-bearers.
7-24.desc: Holy Passion-Bearers Boris and Gleb, princes of Rus'.
7-24.name: Boris and Gleb

7-24.bio:
St. Theophilos was a sailor from Zakynthos who was falsely accused and pressured to embrace Islam. Tradition relates that he repented of a moment of weakness and boldly confessed Christ in Chios.

He was burned alive in 1635 and is honored among the New Martyrs.
7-24.desc: New Martyr Theophilos of Zakynthos, who suffered in Chios.
7-24.name: Theophilos of Zakynthos

7-24.bio:
St. Athanasios was a young Christian from Kios in Bithynia who, tradition relates, was accused before the Ottoman authorities and refused to deny his faith.

He was beheaded in Constantinople in 1670 and is honored among the New Martyrs.
7-24.desc: New Martyr Athanasios of Kios in Bithynia.
7-24.name: Athanasios of Kios

7-24.bio:
Sts. Kapiton, Hymenaios and Hermogenes are commemorated together as martyrs who confessed Christ during the persecutions of the early Church. Tradition relates that they died by the sword.

Their names are preserved in the Synaxarion.
7-24.desc: Holy Martyrs Kapiton, Hymenaios and Hermogenes.
7-24.name: Kapiton, Hymenaios and Hermogenes

7-25.bio:
On July 25 the Church commemorates the Dormition of St. Anna, the mother of the Most Holy Theotokos. With her husband, the righteous Joachim, she bore childlessness with patience and prayer until God granted them in old age the daughter who would become the Mother of God. According to tradition she reposed in peace in Jerusalem.

St. Anna is honored as the grandmother of Christ according to the flesh, and is invoked by mothers, by married couples, and by those praying to be granted children. The feast is the principal name day of those named Anna.
7-25.desc: Dormition of Saint Anne, mother of the Theotokos.
7-25.name: Dormition of Anne

7-25.bio:
St. Olympias was a noblewoman of Constantinople who, widowed young, devoted her great wealth to the Church and the poor and was ordained a deaconess. She was a close friend and supporter of St. John Chrysostom, and shared his sufferings when he was exiled.

She herself was persecuted and exiled, and reposed in the early fifth century. Chrysostom's letters to her are preserved.
7-25.desc: Venerable Olympias the Deaconess of Constantinople, friend of St. John Chrysostom.
7-25.name: Olympias the Deaconess

7-25.bio:
St. Eupraxia was born to a noble family related to Emperor Theodosios the Great. As a child she entered a convent in the Thebaid of Egypt with her mother and, refusing the marriage arranged for her, remained there in great asceticism and humility.

Tradition relates that she was granted the gift of healing, and she reposed in the early fifth century.
7-25.desc: Venerable Eupraxia, virgin of the Thebaid.
7-25.name: Eupraxia of Tabenna

7-25.bio:
The Fifth Ecumenical Council met in Constantinople in 553 under Emperor Justinian and condemned the errors of Origen and the so-called Three Chapters, confirming the teaching of Chalcedon.

The Church honors its 165 Fathers as defenders of the Orthodox faith.
7-25.desc: Commemoration of the 165 Holy Fathers of the Fifth Ecumenical Council in Constantinople.
7-25.name: Fathers of the Fifth Ecumenical Council

7-25.bio:
Sts. Sanctus, Maturus, Attalus and Blandina were among the Christians of Lyon in Gaul who suffered in the persecution of 177. Blandina, a slave girl, endured every torment with such courage that she strengthened all the others, and was the last to die.

Their martyrdom is described in a letter preserved by Eusebius.
7-25.desc: Holy Martyrs Sanctus, Maturus, Attalus and Blandina of Lyon in Gaul.
7-25.name: Blandina and the Martyrs of Lyon

7-25.bio:
St. Gregory Kallidis was born in 1844 near Silivria and served as a hierarch of the Ecumenical Patriarchate, finally as Metropolitan of Heraclea in Thrace. He was known for his charity, his learning and his pastoral care.

He reposed in Thessaloniki in 1925 and was glorified in 2003.
7-25.desc: St. Gregory Kallidis, Metropolitan of Heraclea, hierarch of the twentieth century.
7-25.name: Gregory Kallidis

7-26.bio:
St. Paraskevi was born near Rome in the second century to devout Christian parents, who named her for the day of the Passion of the Lord, Friday, in Greek Paraskevi. After their death she gave her goods to the poor and went about preaching Christ, for which she was arrested; she endured torture with steadfastness and was finally beheaded, her witness, according to tradition, bringing even her persecutors to wonder.

She is one of the most beloved women saints of Greece, and because tradition tells of healing granted through her to the eyes of a persecutor, she is invoked especially for diseases of sight. Her feast is July 26.
7-26.name: Paraskevi the Great Martyr

7-26.bio:
St. Hermolaos was a priest of Nicomedia who survived the burning of the twenty thousand martyrs and lived in hiding, where he instructed the young Panteleimon in the faith and baptized him. Denounced during the trial of Panteleimon, he confessed Christ together with Hermippos and Hermokrates.

All three were beheaded shortly before the martyrdom of St. Panteleimon.
7-26.desc: Hieromartyr Hermolaos and Martyrs Hermippos and Hermokrates of Nicomedia.
7-26.name: Hermolaos, Hermippos and Hermokrates

7-26.bio:
St. Oraiozele was, according to tradition, a disciple of the Apostle Andrew who confessed Christ in the region of Byzantium. She was tortured and beheaded for her faith.

She is honored as a virgin martyr of the apostolic age.
7-26.desc: Holy Virgin Martyr Oraiozele, disciple of the Apostle Andrew.
7-26.name: Oraiozele the Virgin Martyr

7-26.bio:
St. Ierousalem was a Christian woman of Berroia in Macedonia who, tradition relates, was martyred together with her children for her confession of Christ.

She is honored as a martyr of the early Church in Berroia.
7-26.name: Ierousalem the Martyr

7-26.bio:
St. Gerontios was an ascetic of Mount Athos who is honored as the founder of the Skete of St. Anne, the oldest and largest of the Athonite sketes. Tradition relates that he lived in the fourteenth century.

He reposed in peace and is honored among the saints of the Holy Mountain.
7-26.desc: Venerable Gerontios, founder of the Skete of St. Anne on Mount Athos.
7-26.name: Gerontios of Athos

7-26.bio:
St. Jacob Netsvetov was born in Alaska to a Russian father and an Aleut mother and was the first native Alaskan ordained to the priesthood. For decades he traveled the Aleutian Islands and the Yukon, translating the Scriptures and baptizing thousands.

He reposed in 1864 and was glorified in 1994.
7-26.desc: St. Jacob Netsvetov, priest and enlightener of the peoples of Alaska.
7-26.name: Jacob Netsvetov of Alaska

7-27.bio:
St. Panteleimon the Great Martyr and Healer was born in Nicomedia in the late third century. Trained as a physician, he was brought to Christ by the priest St. Hermolaos, and thereafter healed the sick freely in the name of the Lord, taking no payment, for which he is counted among the Holy Unmercenaries. Denounced during the persecution of Maximian, he endured many tortures and was beheaded around the year 305.

His name means all-merciful. He is invoked above all for the sick, and physicians and nurses honor him as their patron. His feast on July 27 is kept with devotion throughout the Orthodox world.
7-27.desc: Great Martyr and Unmercenary Panteleimon of Nicomedia.
7-27.name: Panteleimon the Unmercenary

7-27.bio:
St. Anthousa was an abbess in the eighth century who defended the veneration of the holy icons during the iconoclast persecution. Tradition relates that she was tortured and exiled by the emperor Constantine Copronymus.

She returned to her convent and reposed in peace as a confessor.
7-27.desc: Venerable Anthousa the Confessor, abbess who suffered for the holy icons.
7-27.name: Anthousa the Confessor

7-27.bio:
St. Christodoulos was from Kassandra in Chalkidiki and worked as a tailor in Thessaloniki. Tradition relates that, grieved by the apostasy of a Christian, he openly confessed Christ before the Ottoman judge.

He was hanged in Thessaloniki in 1777 and is honored among the New Martyrs.
7-27.desc: New Martyr Christodoulos of Kassandra, who suffered in Thessaloniki.
7-27.name: Christodoulos of Kassandra

7-27.bio:
The 153 Martyrs of Thrace were Christians who confessed Christ during the persecutions. Tradition relates that they were drowned in the sea for their faith.

The Church keeps their common memory.
7-27.desc: The Holy 153 Martyrs of Thrace, drowned in the sea.
7-27.name: One Hundred Fifty-Three Martyrs of Thrace

7-27.bio:
St. Nicholas Kochanov was born to a wealthy family of Novgorod and took up the ascetic life of a fool for Christ, enduring mockery for the Lord's sake. Tradition relates that he and the fool Theodore feigned quarrels across the river to shame the feuding citizens.

He reposed in 1392 and is honored as a wonderworker.
7-27.desc: Blessed Nicholas Kochanov, Fool for Christ of Novgorod.
7-27.name: Nicholas Kochanov of Novgorod

7-28.bio:
St. Prokoros was one of the Seven Deacons chosen by the Apostles in Jerusalem to serve the needs of the growing Church, as recorded in the Acts of the Apostles. According to tradition he became a devoted disciple and companion of St. John the Theologian, accompanying him in his labors and, as tradition holds, serving as his scribe.

He is said to have later served as bishop of Nicomedia and to have completed his course as a martyr. He is commemorated on July 28.
7-28.name: Prokoros the Apostle

7-28.bio:
St. Irene was a noblewoman of Cappadocia in the ninth century who, on her way to Constantinople to be considered as bride of the emperor, chose instead the monastic life at the convent of Chrysovalantou. She became abbess and was renowned for asceticism, discernment and miracles.

Tradition relates that a sailor brought her three apples from Paradise, and her blessed apples are still given to the faithful. She reposed in peace at a great age and is deeply loved throughout the Greek world.
7-28.desc: Venerable Irene, abbess of Chrysovalantou, wonderworker.
7-28.name: Irene Chrysovalantou

7-28.bio:
St. Paul of Xeropotamou was, according to tradition, of imperial lineage and renounced the world to live as an ascetic on Mount Athos in the tenth century. He founded the Monastery of Xeropotamou and later the Monastery of St. Paul, which bears his name.

He reposed in peace and is honored among the founders of Athonite monasticism.
7-28.desc: Venerable Paul, founder of the Monastery of Xeropotamou on Mount Athos.
7-28.name: Paul of Xeropotamou

7-28.bio:
St. Eustathios was a soldier who confessed Christ in Ancyra of Galatia during the persecutions. Tradition relates that he was tortured and thrown into the river, but was preserved and later gave up his soul in peace.

He is commemorated as a martyr of Ancyra.
7-28.desc: Holy Martyr Eustathios, who suffered in Ancyra.
7-28.name: Eustathios of Ancyra

7-28.bio:
St. Drosis is commemorated on this day as a woman martyr who confessed Christ during the persecutions. Tradition relates that she died by the sword.

Her name is preserved in the Synaxarion among the martyrs of this day.
7-28.name: Drosis the Martyr

7-28.bio:
St. Akakios was a Christian who confessed Christ before the governor in Apamea and endured many tortures. Tradition relates that he was finally beheaded.

He is honored as a martyr of the early Church.
7-28.desc: Holy Martyr Akakios, who suffered in Apamea.
7-28.name: Akakios the Martyr

7-29.bio:
St. Kallinikos was a Christian of Asia Minor who traveled from place to place preaching Christ and turning many from the worship of idols. Seized during the persecutions, he was brought to Gangra in Paphlagonia, where after cruel torments he was condemned to death by fire, and gave up his soul to God with thanksgiving.

His name means one of beautiful victory, and the Church honors in him the triumph of faith over suffering. He is commemorated on July 29.
7-29.name: Kallinikos

7-29.bio:
St. Theodote was a Christian widow of Nicaea in Bithynia who, with her three young sons, was arrested for the faith during the persecution of Diocletian. Tradition relates that she encouraged her children to remain steadfast.

Mother and children were burned together, receiving the crown of martyrdom as one family.
7-29.desc: Holy Martyr Theodote and her three children, who suffered in Bithynia.
7-29.name: Theodote and her Three Children

7-29.bio:
St. Theodosios the Younger was Emperor of the East from 408 to 450, the son of Arcadius and grandson of Theodosios the Great. He was known for piety and learning, and during his reign the Third Ecumenical Council was convened at Ephesus.

He reposed in peace and is honored among the right-believing emperors.
7-29.name: Theodosios the Younger

7-29.bio:
St. John the Soldier served in the army of the emperor Julian the Apostate and was ordered to persecute Christians; instead he secretly helped them, warning them and aiding the poor. Imprisoned for this, he was freed after Julian's death and lived out his days in works of mercy.

He is invoked in prayer against thieves and for the finding of lost things.
7-29.desc: Holy Martyr John the Soldier, protector of the wronged.
7-29.name: John the Soldier

7-29.bio:
St. Basiliskos the Elder is commemorated as a martyr who confessed Christ during the persecutions. Tradition relates that he died by fire.

His name is preserved in the Synaxarion among the martyrs of this day.
7-29.name: Basiliskos the Elder

7-29.bio:
Sts. Benjamin and Berios are commemorated together as martyrs who confessed Christ during the persecutions of the early Church. Tradition relates that they died by the sword.

Their names are preserved in the Synaxarion.
7-29.name: Benjamin and Berios

7-3.bio:
St. Hyakinthos was a young Christian of Caesarea in Cappadocia who served at the imperial court in the time of the Emperor Trajan. When his faith became known, he refused to eat food offered to idols, and for his confession of Christ he was imprisoned and died in his bonds, still in his youth, receiving the crown of martyrdom.

His steadfastness at so young an age has made him an example of purity of conscience, keeping the faith even in small things. He is commemorated on July 3.
7-3.name: Hyakinthos

7-3.bio:
St. Anatolios was born in Alexandria and served as Patriarch of Constantinople in the fifth century. He took part in the Fourth Ecumenical Council at Chalcedon, which confirmed the Orthodox teaching on the two natures of Christ.

He is also remembered as a hymnographer, and reposed in peace after governing the Church of Constantinople with wisdom.
7-3.desc: St. Anatolios, Patriarch of Constantinople, who presided at the Fourth Ecumenical Council.
7-3.name: Anatolios of Constantinople

7-3.bio:
St. Gerasimos the New was a young man from Karpenisi in central Greece who worked in Constantinople. Tradition relates that he was pressured to convert to Islam and, having briefly wavered, repented and boldly confessed Christ before the authorities.

He was beheaded for his confession in 1812 and is honored among the New Martyrs of the Ottoman period.
7-3.desc: New Martyr Gerasimos of Karpenisi, who suffered in Constantinople.
7-3.name: Gerasimos the New of Karpenisi

7-3.bio:
Sts. Theodotos and Theodote, together with Golinduch, Diomedes, Eulampios and Asklepiades, are commemorated as a company of martyrs who confessed Christ during the persecutions of the early Church. Tradition relates that they suffered in Caesarea of Cappadocia.

Refusing to sacrifice to idols, they endured tortures and received the crown of martyrdom together.
7-3.desc: Holy Martyrs Theodotos, Theodote, Golinduch, Diomedes, Eulampios and Asklepiades.
7-3.name: Theodotos, Theodote and those with them

7-3.bio:
Sts. Mark and Mokianos were Christians who refused to offer sacrifice to the pagan gods when commanded by the governor. Tradition relates that they were beheaded for their confession of Christ.

The Synaxarion also recalls that the mother of Mokianos encouraged her son to remain steadfast until the end.
7-3.desc: Holy Martyrs Mark and Mokianos, beheaded for refusing to worship idols.
7-3.name: Mark and Mokianos

7-3.bio:
St. Basil served as Bishop of Murom and later Ryazan in the thirteenth century. Tradition relates that, slandered by his flock in Murom, he set out on the river on his cloak and was miraculously carried to Ryazan, where he was received with honor.

He reposed in 1295 and is venerated as a wonderworker of the Russian Church.
7-3.desc: St. Basil, Bishop of Ryazan and Murom, wonderworker of the thirteenth century.
7-3.name: Basil of Ryazan

7-30.bio:
St. Silas, numbered among the Seventy Apostles, was a leading man of the Church in Jerusalem who was chosen to accompany St. Paul on his missionary journeys. He shared the Apostle's labors and sufferings, and at Philippi was imprisoned with him, praying and singing hymns at midnight when the earthquake opened the prison doors.

According to tradition he later served as bishop of Corinth, completing his apostolic course in faithfulness. He is commemorated with his fellow apostles on July 30.
7-30.desc: Holy Apostle Silas, companion of Paul.
7-30.name: Silas the Apostle

7-30.bio:
Sts. Silouanos, Epainetos, Kreskes and Andronikos are numbered among the Seventy Apostles and are mentioned in the Epistles of St. Paul. Silouanos became bishop of Thessaloniki, Kreskes preached in Galatia, Epainetos was bishop of Carthage, and Andronikos labored in Pannonia.

They are commemorated together with the Apostle Silas on this day.
7-30.desc: Holy Apostles Silouanos, Epainetos, Kreskes and Andronikos of the Seventy, fellow-workers of St. Paul.
7-30.name: Silouanos, Epainetos, Kreskes and Andronikos

7-30.bio:
St. Julitta was a wealthy Christian widow of Caesarea in Cappadocia whose property was seized by a pagan. When she sought justice, she was told to renounce Christ; she refused and was condemned to the fire.

St. Basil the Great preached a homily in her honor, praising her courage.
7-30.desc: Holy Martyr Julitta of Caesarea in Cappadocia.
7-30.name: Julitta of Caesarea

7-30.bio:
St. Valentinos was Bishop of Interamna (Terni) in Italy in the third century, known for healing the sick. Tradition relates that his healing of a young man led to the conversion of several pagan youths, who were martyred with him.

He was beheaded at Rome and is commemorated on this day in the Orthodox calendar.
7-30.desc: Hieromartyr Valentinos, Bishop of Interamna in Italy, and those with him.
7-30.name: Valentinos of Interamna

7-31.bio:
St. Eudokimos the Righteous was born in Cappadocia in the ninth century to devout parents. Serving as an officer in the imperial service, he lived in the midst of the world a life of hidden holiness, guarding purity, giving alms generously to the poor and to widows and orphans, and avoiding all display, with a special reverence for the Theotokos.

He reposed while still young, and God glorified his hidden virtue, for his relics were found incorrupt and wrought healings. His name means one of good repute, and he is commemorated on July 31.
7-31.desc: St. Eudokimos the Righteous of Cappadocia.
7-31.name: Eudokimos the Righteous

7-31.bio:
Righteous Joseph of Arimathea was a member of the Sanhedrin and a secret disciple of Christ who boldly asked Pilate for the Lord's body, wrapped it in linen and laid it in his own new tomb. He is commemorated in the hymns of Holy Saturday and the Myrrhbearers.

Tradition relates that he later preached the Gospel far from Judea and reposed in peace.
7-31.desc: Righteous Joseph of Arimathea, who buried the body of the Lord.
7-31.name: Joseph of Arimathea

7-31.bio:
The Twelve Martyrs of Rome are commemorated together as Christians who confessed Christ in the imperial city during the persecutions. Tradition relates that they were beheaded.

The Church keeps their common memory.
7-31.desc: The Holy Twelve Martyrs of Rome, who died by the sword.
7-31.name: Twelve Martyrs of Rome

7-31.bio:
This New Martyr was a young Cretan whose name has not been preserved. Tradition relates that, having been forced into apostasy, he repented and confessed Christ before the authorities in Alexandria of Egypt.

He was beheaded in 1811 and is honored among the New Martyrs of Crete.
7-31.desc: The unnamed New Martyr of Crete, who suffered in Alexandria.
7-31.name: Anonymous New Martyr of Crete

7-4.bio:
St. Andrew of Crete was born in Damascus in the seventh century. First a monk in Jerusalem, he later served in Constantinople and was consecrated Archbishop of Gortyna in Crete, where he shepherded his flock with wisdom and care for the poor.

He is honored above all as a hymnographer, the author of the Great Canon of repentance, which the Church sings during Great Lent as one of her most profound calls to compunction. He reposed in the first half of the eighth century and is commemorated on July 4.
7-4.name: Andrew the Apostle of Crete

7-4.bio:
St. Michael Choniates was a learned churchman from Chonae in Asia Minor who became Metropolitan of Athens in the late twelfth century. He cared devotedly for his impoverished flock and defended the city against the oppressions of tax collectors and local lords.

After the Latin conquest of Athens in 1204 he lived in exile on the island of Kea, continuing to guide his people by letter until his repose.
7-4.desc: St. Michael Choniates, Metropolitan of Athens, scholar and shepherd of the city.
7-4.name: Michael Choniates of Athens

7-4.bio:
St. Theodore was Bishop of Cyrene in Libya during the persecution of Diocletian. A skilled copyist of the Scriptures, he was denounced to the governor and tortured for his faith.

Tradition relates that his sufferings led others, including the women Kyprilla, Aroa and Lucia, to confess Christ, and that he reposed from his wounds.
7-4.desc: Hieromartyr Theodore, Bishop of Cyrene in Libya.
7-4.name: Theodore of Cyrene

7-4.bio:
Sts. Kyprilla, Aroa and Lucia were Christian women of Cyrene in Libya who were moved by the sufferings of Bishop Theodore to confess Christ openly. Tradition relates that Kyprilla was a widow who had been healed through the bishop.

They were tortured and received the crown of martyrdom in the persecution of Diocletian.
7-4.desc: Holy Women Martyrs Kyprilla, Aroa and Lucia of Cyrene.
7-4.name: Kyprilla, Aroa and Lucia

7-4.bio:
St. Martha was a pious woman of Antioch in the sixth century and the mother of St. Symeon Stylites the Younger of the Wonderful Mountain. After her husband's death she gave herself to prayer, fasting and works of mercy.

She reposed in peace and was buried near her son's pillar, where tradition relates that many were healed at her tomb.
7-4.desc: Venerable Martha of Antioch, mother of St. Symeon Stylites the Younger.
7-4.name: Martha, Mother of Symeon the Stylite

7-4.bio:
St. Andrei Rublev was a monk of the Holy Trinity Monastery of St. Sergius near Moscow in the late fourteenth and early fifteenth centuries. He is the most renowned of Russian iconographers, and his icon of the Holy Trinity is honored throughout the Orthodox world.

He reposed in peace at the Andronikov Monastery and was glorified as a saint by the Russian Church.
7-4.desc: Venerable Andrei Rublev, monk and iconographer of the Holy Trinity Lavra.
7-4.name: Andrei Rublev the Iconographer

7-5.bio:
St. Athanasios the Athonite was born in Trebizond in the tenth century. Drawn from a promising career in Constantinople to the monastic life, he came to Mount Athos and there founded the Great Lavra, the first of the great communal monasteries of the Holy Mountain, with the support of the Emperor Nikephoros Phokas.

Under his guidance Athos grew into the chief center of Orthodox monasticism, as it remains to this day. According to tradition he ended his earthly life during the collapse of a church structure under construction at the Lavra. He is commemorated on July 5.
7-5.desc: Founder of the Great Lavra of Mount Athos.
7-5.name: Athanasios of Athos

7-5.bio:
St. Lampados was an ascetic of Irenopolis in Isauria, distinguished for wisdom, gentleness and humility. Tradition relates that he lived in a cave in strict asceticism and was granted the gift of working miracles.

He reposed in peace and is honored as a wonderworker.
7-5.desc: Venerable Lampados the Wonderworker of Irenopolis.
7-5.name: Lampados of Irenopolis

7-5.bio:
St. Kyprianos was a monk of Koutloumousiou Monastery on Mount Athos who, burning with zeal, went to Thessaloniki and then Constantinople to preach Christ to the Muslims. Refusing to renounce his faith, he was beheaded in 1679.

He is honored among the New Martyrs of the Holy Mountain.
7-5.desc: New Monastic Martyr Kyprianos of Koutloumousiou, who suffered in Constantinople.
7-5.name: Kyprianos the New Martyr

7-5.bio:
St. Stephen is honored as an early bishop of Rhegium (Reggio) in Calabria, southern Italy. Tradition relates that he was ordained by the Apostle Paul and suffered martyrdom for the faith.

He is venerated as the patron of the Church of Reggio Calabria.
7-5.desc: Hieromartyr Stephen, Bishop of Rhegium in Calabria.
7-5.name: Stephen of Rhegium

7-5.bio:
This day commemorates the uncovering of the relics of St. Sergius of Radonezh at the Holy Trinity Monastery in 1422, some thirty years after his repose. His relics were found incorrupt and became a source of healings.

St. Sergius is the most beloved of Russian monastic saints, whose main feast is kept on September 25.
7-5.desc: Uncovering of the relics of Venerable Sergius of Radonezh, abbot of the Holy Trinity Lavra.
7-5.name: Finding of the Relics of Sergius of Radonezh

7-5.bio:
On this day the Church of Crete honors together all the saints of the island: apostles, hierarchs, martyrs, ascetics and New Martyrs, from the Apostle Titus to those who suffered under the Ottomans.

The synaxis gathers the many local saints of Crete into a single celebration.
7-5.desc: Synaxis of all the Saints who have shone forth in Crete.
7-5.name: Synaxis of All Saints of Crete

7-6.bio:
St. Sisoes the Great was one of the renowned desert fathers of Egypt, living in the fourth and fifth centuries. After years in Sketis he withdrew to the mountain where St. Anthony the Great had lived, and there spent long decades in solitude, prayer, and profound humility, receiving those who came for a word of salvation.

His sayings, preserved among the fathers, breathe repentance and gentleness; at the end of his life he confessed that he did not know if he had even begun to repent. He is commemorated on July 6.
7-6.name: Sisoes the Great

7-6.bio:
St. Lucia was a virgin from Campania in Italy who was taken captive and brought before the vicar Rixos. Tradition relates that he was so moved by her faith and austere life that he himself became a Christian.

Lucia, Rixos and many others were martyred together at Rome.
7-6.desc: Holy Virgin Martyr Lucia of Campania, with Rixos the vicar and many others.
7-6.name: Lucia the Virgin Martyr and those with her

7-6.bio:
St. Asteios was Bishop of Dyrrachium (Durres) in the reign of Trajan. Tradition relates that he was smeared with honey and hung in the sun to be tormented by insects for refusing to sacrifice to idols.

He died in his sufferings and is honored as a hieromartyr and patron of Durres.
7-6.name: Asteios of Dyrrachium

7-6.bio:
Sts. Philemon, Archippus and Onesimus are known from the Epistle of the Apostle Paul to Philemon. Philemon was a Christian of Colossae, Archippus a fellow-worker, and Onesimus the runaway slave whom Paul sent back as a brother in Christ.

Tradition relates that they later suffered martyrdom for the Gospel; they are commemorated on several days of the year.
7-6.desc: Holy Apostles Philemon, Archippus and Onesimus of the Seventy.
7-6.name: Philemon, Archippus and Onesimus

7-6.bio:
St. Kyrillos was a monk from Thessaloniki who confessed Christ before the Ottoman authorities. Tradition relates that he was burned alive in Thessaloniki in the sixteenth century.

He is honored among the New Martyrs of the Ottoman period.
7-6.desc: New Monastic Martyr Kyrillos, who suffered in Thessaloniki.
7-6.name: Kyrillos of Thessaloniki

7-6.bio:
The Twenty-Four Martyrs are commemorated together as a company of Christians who confessed Christ in the time of persecution. Tradition relates that they were put to the sword.

Their names are not preserved, but the Church keeps their common memory.
7-6.desc: The Holy Twenty-Four Martyrs who died by the sword.
7-6.name: Twenty-Four Martyrs

7-7.bio:
St. Thomas of Maloea was, according to tradition, a man of prominence and strength in the world who left all things to become a monk, taking up the life of prayer and ascetic struggle on Mount Maloea. There he lived in stillness, and God glorified his hidden labors with the grace of wonderworking.

The synaxaria preserve little else of his life beyond his renunciation of the world and his holiness in the desert. He is commemorated on July 7.
7-7.name: Thomas of Maloea

7-7.bio:
St. Kyriaki was born in Nicomedia to Christian parents, Dorotheos and Eusebia, who had long prayed for a child; she was named for the Lord's Day on which she was born. Beautiful and devout, she refused marriage, dedicating herself to Christ, and was denounced during the persecution of Diocletian.

She endured many tortures with steadfastness, and tradition relates that she gave up her soul in prayer before the executioner's sword could fall. She is one of the most beloved women saints of the Greek people.
7-7.desc: Holy Great Martyr Kyriaki of Nicomedia, virgin, who suffered under Diocletian.
7-7.name: Kyriaki the Great Martyr

7-7.bio:
St. Vlasios was a priest and monk of Sklavaina in Akarnania, western Greece, who lived in the eleventh century. Tradition relates that he and his companions were killed by Saracen pirates who raided their monastery.

His memory was revealed in modern times through visions, and his relics are honored in Akarnania.
7-7.desc: Hieromartyr Vlasios of Sklavaina in Akarnania and his companions, slain by pirates.
7-7.name: Vlasios of Akarnania and those with him

7-7.bio:
St. Eustathios is commemorated as a hieromartyr, a priest who confessed Christ during the persecutions of the early Church. Tradition relates that he was put to death for his faith.

His name is kept in the Synaxarion together with the other martyrs of this day.
7-7.desc: Hieromartyr Eustathios, who suffered for Christ.
7-7.name: Eustathios the Hieromartyr

7-7.bio:
St. Polykarpos the New is commemorated as a martyr who confessed Christ and suffered for the faith. He is called 'the New' to distinguish him from the great Hieromartyr Polycarp of Smyrna.

Tradition relates that he died by the sword.
7-7.name: Polykarpos the New

7-7.bio:
St. Evangelos is honored as an early bishop of Tomis on the Black Sea, in present-day Romania. Tradition relates that he preached the Gospel in the region and was beheaded for his confession of Christ in the third century.

He is commemorated as a martyr, and his day is kept by many who bear his name.
7-7.desc: Holy Martyr Evangelos, bishop of Tomis, who died by the sword.
7-7.name: Evangelos the Martyr

7-7.bio:
Sts. Peregrinos, Lucian, Pompeius, Hesychios, Papias, Saturninus and Germanus were Christians from Italy who fled the persecution of Trajan to Dyrrachium. There, seeing the sufferings of the bishop Asteios, they openly confessed Christ.

They were drowned in the sea for their faith, and their bodies were later found and buried with honor.
7-7.desc: Holy Martyrs Peregrinos, Lucian, Pompeius, Hesychios, Papias, Saturninus and Germanus of Dyrrachium.
7-7.name: Peregrinos and those with him

7-8.bio:
St. Procopios the Great Martyr suffered for Christ at Caesarea in Palestine during the persecution of Diocletian at the beginning of the fourth century. According to tradition he was first a persecutor of Christians, but was converted by a divine revelation, confessed Christ openly, and endured imprisonment and torture before being beheaded.

He is numbered among the great military martyrs of the Church, and many churches in the Greek world bear his name. His feast is kept on July 8.
7-8.name: Procopios

7-8.bio:
St. Theophilos was born in Macedonia in the fifteenth century and, after serving the Church in Thessaloniki and Constantinople, withdrew to Mount Athos. He lived in asceticism at Vatopedi and the skete of St. Basil, and reposed in 1548.

After his repose his relics flowed with myrrh, for which he is called the Myrrh-gusher.
7-8.desc: Venerable Theophilos the Myrrh-gusher of Mount Athos.
7-8.name: Theophilos the Myrrh-gusher

7-8.bio:
St. Anastasios, called Gounaras, the Furrier, was from the village of Agios Vlasios near Thessaloniki. Tradition relates that after falling into apostasy he repented and boldly confessed Christ in Constantinople.

He was beheaded in 1743 and is honored among the New Martyrs.
7-8.desc: New Martyr Anastasios the Furrier from Agios Vlasios, who suffered in Constantinople.
7-8.name: Anastasios the New Martyr of Agios Vlasios

7-8.bio:
St. Theodosia was the mother of the Great Martyr Procopios. Tradition relates that although at first a pagan, she was converted by her son's steadfastness under torture and confessed Christ herself.

She was beheaded together with the twelve senatorial women who had believed through Procopios.
7-8.desc: Holy Martyr Theodosia, mother of the Great Martyr Procopios.
7-8.name: Theodosia, Mother of Procopios

7-8.bio:
Sts. Antiochos and Nikostratos were military tribunes in Caesarea of Palestine who, together with their soldiers, came to faith through the witness of the Great Martyr Procopios. Tradition relates that they were baptized and shortly afterwards beheaded.

They are commemorated with St. Procopios and the others who suffered with him.
7-8.desc: Holy Martyrs Antiochos and Nikostratos, tribunes converted by St. Procopios.
7-8.name: Antiochos and Nikostratos the Tribunes

7-8.bio:
St. Procopios was a merchant from the West who embraced Orthodoxy in Novgorod and took up the ascetic life of a fool for Christ in Ustyug. He lived in poverty and prayer and was despised by many during his life.

Tradition relates that his prayers saved the city from a storm of fiery stones. He reposed in 1303 and is honored as a wonderworker.
7-8.desc: Blessed Procopios, Fool for Christ and wonderworker of Ustyug.
7-8.name: Procopios of Ustyug

7-9.bio:
St. Pancratius was, according to tradition, a disciple of the apostles who was sent to Sicily and became the first bishop of Tauromenium, present-day Taormina. There he preached the Gospel, overturned the worship of idols, and gathered a flock for Christ in the earliest days of the Church.

He completed his ministry as a martyr, put to death by enemies of the faith. He is honored as one of the apostolic founders of the Church in Sicily, and is commemorated on July 9.
7-9.name: Pancratius of Tauromenion

7-9.bio:
St. Michael Paknanas was a young gardener of Athens who was falsely accused and pressured to convert to Islam. He refused steadfastly, answering that he would not deny his faith.

He was beheaded in Athens in 1771 and is honored as one of the New Martyrs of the city.
7-9.desc: New Martyr Michael Paknanas the Gardener of Athens.
7-9.name: Michael Paknanas the Gardener

7-9.bio:
St. Dionysios the Rhetor was a learned monk of Mount Athos who settled in the Little Skete of St. Anne in the early seventeenth century. His disciple Metrophanes, a spiritual father, labored with him in asceticism.

Both reposed in peace and are honored among the saints of the Holy Mountain.
7-9.desc: Venerable Dionysios the Rhetor and his disciple Metrophanes of the Skete of St. Anne.
7-9.name: Dionysios the Rhetor and Metrophanes

7-9.bio:
St. Photios was an ascetic who founded the Monastery of Akapniou in Thessaloniki. Tradition relates that he lived in the tenth or eleventh century and was known for his holiness and spiritual guidance.

He reposed in peace and was honored by the monastery he founded.
7-9.desc: Venerable Photios, founder of the Akapniou Monastery in Thessaloniki.
7-9.name: Photios of Akapniou

7-9.bio:
Sts. Andrew and Probos are commemorated as martyrs who confessed Christ during the persecutions. Tradition relates that they were burned for their faith.

The Synaxarion keeps their names among the martyrs of this day.
7-9.desc: Holy Martyrs Andrew and Probos, who died by fire.
7-9.name: Andrew and Probos
